# TradieInsurance.co.nz

> Specialist tradie insurance comparison and broker referral service for New Zealand. We connect tradies with licensed insurance advisers to find the right cover for their trade.

## About This Site

TradieInsurance.co.nz is an information and referral service for tradies seeking insurance cover. We provide general information about tradie insurance options and connect users with licensed insurance brokers and advisers regulated under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (FMCA).

**Important:** TradieInsurance.co.nz is NOT a licensed financial adviser and does NOT provide financial advice. All insurance quotes and recommendations are provided by the licensed brokers and advisers we refer you to. Those brokers hold Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licences.

## Contact

- Email: hello@cover4you.co.nz
- Website: https://www.tradieinsurance.co.nz

## Core Coverage Types

Premiums are set by each insurer on the business's details (turnover, staff, trade, limits, claims history). This site does not publish prices.

| Cover Type | Who Needs It |
|---|---|
| Public Liability | All tradies working on client sites |
| Tools & Equipment | Any tradie with valuable tools |
| Commercial Vehicle | Tradies using vehicles for work |
| Income Protection | Self-employed tradies without sick pay |
| Statutory Liability | Employers, high-risk site workers (defence costs; fines under HSWA and the RMA cannot be insured) |
| Professional Indemnity | LBPs doing design work, design-build, certifiers |
| Contents & Property | Tradies with workshop or depot |
| Building Insurance | Business owners with commercial premises |

## Trade Types Covered

- Builders (including Licensed Building Practitioners)
- Plumbers and Gasfitters
- Painters and Decorators
- Carpenters and Woodworkers
- Electricians
- Bricklayers and Blocklayers
- Roofers
- Concreters
- Handymen
- Gasfitters (standalone licensed gasfitting)
- Tilers (floor and wall tiling)
- Glaziers (glass installation and replacement)
- Landscapers (garden design, earthworks, irrigation)
- Drain Layers (stormwater, sewage, drainage)
- Scaffolders (construction scaffolding erection)
- Fencers (boundary and rural fencing)
- Plasterers (interior and exterior plaster systems)
- HVAC Technicians (heating, ventilation, and refrigeration)
- Arborists (tree surgery and arboriculture)
- Welders (metal fabrication and structural welding)
- Irrigation Specialists (agricultural and commercial irrigation)

## Regulatory and Compliance Information

- All referred brokers are licensed under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (FMCA)
- Brokers hold Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licences issued by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA)
- ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) covers workplace injuries — income protection covers illness and non-work injuries
- Fines under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 cannot be insured (s29); statutory liability can cover defence costs
- Resource Management Act fines imposed after 20 August 2025 cannot be insured; defence and remediation costs still can
- Building Act 2004: residential work of $30,000+ (incl GST) needs a written contract and a disclosure statement that sets out the contractor's insurance, amounts and relevant exclusions
- WorkSafe NZ is the regulator for workplace health and safety
- Public liability limits are usually set by the contract; head contractors and commercial clients commonly specify a minimum

## Frequently Asked Questions Summary

- How much does tradie insurance cost? It depends on turnover, staff, trade, limits and claims history; each insurer prices it differently.
- Is tradie insurance legally required? Generally not by law, but construction companies, head contractors and commercial clients routinely require public liability before work starts.
- Does ACC cover self-employed tradies? For accidents yes, not illness — income protection fills the gap.
- What level of public liability do I need? Start with the minimum your contracts set, then consider the value of the property you work on.

The insurance brokers and advisers we refer users to are regulated under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. All financial advice and insurance quotes are provided by those licensed advisers, not by this website. See /disclaimer/ for full details.
